subsystems.name: Fungal inoculum
subsystems.role: provides living hyphae that digest the waste and bind it into a solid mass.
parts: selected fungal strain (e.g. oyster mushroom or turkey tail)

subsystems.name: Waste substrate
subsystems.role: the agricultural residue that feeds the fungus and forms the bulk of the brick.

subsystems.name: Mould and growth chamber
subsystems.role: shapes the brick and holds the warm, humid, clean conditions the fungus needs.

subsystems.name: Mycelial binder network
subsystems.role: the hyphae wrap around substrate particles and act as a natural glue.

subsystems.name: Heat treatment and drying
subsystems.role: stops fungal growth, kills spores and sets the composite.

subsystems.name: Finishing and protection
subsystems.role: makes the brick water-resistant, fire-safe and ready for building.

subsystems.name: Testing and quality control
subsystems.role: checks strength, density, thermal performance and fire behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the substrate
buildSteps.detail: Agricultural waste is chopped to a uniform size and pasteurised or sterilised to remove competing moulds and bacteria.

buildSteps.title: Inoculate
buildSteps.detail: The cooled substrate is mixed with fungal spawn so the hyphae can spread through it.

buildSteps.title: Fill the moulds
buildSteps.detail: The mixture is packed into brick-shaped moulds, often with a light press to set the density.

buildSteps.title: Incubate
buildSteps.detail: Moulds are kept dark at around 20–25 °C and high humidity for days to weeks while the mycelium grows through and binds the particles.

buildSteps.title: Demould and heat-treat
buildSteps.detail: Bricks are removed and heated to roughly 70–80 °C to kill the fungus and drive off moisture, stopping further growth.

buildSteps.title: Finish and protect
buildSteps.detail: Surfaces may be sanded and coated with a water-resistant or fire-retardant finish, or combined with a structural frame.

buildSteps.title: Test and certify
buildSteps.detail: Samples are tested for compressive strength, density, thermal conductivity and fire performance before use.

buildSteps.title: Assemble
buildSteps.detail: Bricks are laid with mortar or dry-jointed as non-structural infill, insulation or acoustic panels; load-bearing use requires a validated hybrid system.

prerequisites.tech: Fungal strain selection and sterile culture
prerequisites.why: mycology and mushroom farming already provide reliable strains and clean handling methods.
farms produce straw, hemp hurd and other residues in large volumes.
mushroom farms already control temperature, humidity and cleanliness at scale.

prerequisites.tech: Fire and building code standards for bio-composites
prerequisites.why: mycelium composites are being tested, but codes and certifications are still developing.
mycelium absorbs water unless coated, and long-term outdoor performance is not fully proven.
plain mycelium bricks are weak in compression and tension, so they need frames or engineered composites for load-bearing walls.

pathway.milestone: non-structural insulation, acoustic panels, packaging and temporary pavilions
pathway.unlocks: low-carbon, compostable materials for interiors and short-life structures.

pathway.milestone: engineered mycelium composite bricks with coatings and frames for non-load-bearing walls
pathway.unlocks: wider use in low-rise construction as infill and cladding.

pathway.milestone: load-bearing mycelium composites validated by building codes
pathway.unlocks: carbon-negative structural elements for houses and small buildings.

pathway.milestone: mass production integrated with local agricultural waste streams
pathway.unlocks: circular, locally made building materials that displace concrete and fired clay in some applications.
